subject: Conditional inputs not updating UI selectInput component correctly

messages.author: bda90bcea347c4f0
messages.subject: Conditional inputs not updating UI selectInput component correctly
parts:
I'm comparing combinations of variables to each other and comparing a variable to itself doesn't make sense in my application. 
I have variables c("A", "B", "C", "D"), so if I choose "A" for var1, I should see c("B", "C", "D") appear in the selectInput for var2.

This works on initial startup, but each subsequent change to var1 isn't returning the proper results. When debugging, I can see that the options are correct by printing inputList(), but the menu updates end up like this: var1: "B", var2: c("B", "C", "D").  Basically, it looks like output$selectUI isn't being updated. Portions of my code are below.


global.R:
vars <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")

ui.R:
sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("var1", "Var 1:", 
                choices = c("A", "B", "C", "D")),
    htmlOutput("selectUI")
),


server.R:
 inputList <- reactive({
    vars[-grep(input$var1, vars)]
  })
 
varInput1 <- reactive({
    switch(input$var1,
           "A" = 1,
           "B" = 2,
           "C" = 3,
           "D" = 4)
  })

  varInput2 <- reactive({
    switch(input$var2,
           "A" = 1,
           "B" = 2,
           "C" = 3,
           "D" = 4)
  })

 output$selectUI <- renderUI({ 
    selectInput("var2", "Var 2:", inputList())
  })

messages.author: bda90bcea347c4f0
messages.subject: Re: Conditional inputs not updating UI selectInput component correctly
parts:
I've created a sample application in a gist to help in debugging this problem. Apologies for my lack of understanding of reactivity, but this exercise of reproducing my problem seems to be helping me understand the concept better.

The 2nd input updates correctly now, but I always receive an error on startup:
Error in switch(input$input2, A = 1, B = 2, C = 3, D = 4) : 
  EXPR must be a length 1 vector

I think this is because input2 is not yet defined but am not sure how to rectify it - I've added is.null() checks everywhere I thought was necessary. 

The 2nd issue is if you select "B" for input1 while input2 = "B" as well.. you'll notice that results will display in the mainPanel for input1 = B (2) and input2 = B (2) for a second. However, input2 will update shortly after since it's dependent on input1 and should never = B. I added a Sys.Sleep(2) call so that you can see the transition. For those few seconds, input1 = B and input2 = B but input2 should only be A, C, or D. This is causing issues with my actual application because I have a plot showing up for a second that's showing 2 of the same variables plotted against each other before the actual desired plot appears.

runGist("https://gist.github.com/tcash21/6225683")
